root_cause.text: In `drivers/crypto/omap-crypto.c`, `omap_crypto_copy_sg_lists()` miscomputed the allocation size for the `struct scatterlist *new_sg` buffer by using `sizeof(*sg)` instead of `sizeof(*new_sg)`, so it allocated space for an array of pointers rather than scatterlist objects, causing an undersized buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `kmalloc_array(n, sizeof(*sg), GFP_KERNEL)` to `kmalloc_array(n, sizeof(*new_sg), GFP_KERNEL)`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly says the function was “allocating an array of scatterlist pointers, not scatterlist objects, resulting in a 4x too small allocation.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the destination pointer type for the scatterlist allocation size expression.
intent_record.what: In `omap_crypto_copy_sg_lists()`, the `kmalloc_array()` element-size argument was changed from `sizeof(*sg)` to `sizeof(*new_sg)` when allocating `new_sg`.
intent_record.how: This changes the allocation size expression to match the type of the destination pointer explicitly. Since both expressions likely evaluate to the same size, runtime behavior is unchanged in normal cases, but the code is now clearer and less dependent on the unrelated `sg` symbol.

candidates.rationale: This allocates the new scatterlist buffer using sizeof(*sg), which refers to the wrong object type and can under-allocate memory; the root cause is exactly this miscomputed allocation size.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in `omap_crypto_copy_sg_lists()`. The allocation line is `new_sg = kmalloc_array(n, sizeof(*sg), GFP_KERNEL);`. Here `sg` is a `struct scatterlist **`, so `sizeof(*sg)` is the size of a pointer-to-scatterlist, not the size of `struct scatterlist`. This matches the root cause: the buffer is allocated with the wrong element size, making it undersized for an array of scatterlist objects. There is no corrective handling in this snippet (no `sizeof(*new_sg)` or equivalent), so the fix is not present.
